newsitem.title: MALTA: Late-night diplomacy fails to close Middle East gap.
newsitem.headline: Late-night diplomacy fails to close Middle East gap.

text.p: European diplomats on Wednesday held out little hope of a high-level meeting between Israel and Palestinian leaders after late-night diplomacy failed to bridge the divide between the sides.
Dutch diplomats were saying officially that they had not yet ruled out a meeting between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, but others said it was unlikely.

"A meeting has not formally been ruled out by Mr Arafat and there is still a day to go," said a spokesman for the Dutch, organisers of a two-day Euro-Mediterranean conference in Malta that has brought Israeli and Palestinian leaders together for the first time in weeks.

But Palestinian officials were more sceptical. "The chances of a meeting between Mr Levy and the president almost do not exist," Arafat spokesman Marwan Kanafani told Reuters. "The president is not going to meet with Mr Levy because of certain issues that need to be discussed."

The conference -- which brings together the 15 European Union states and 12 Mediterranean partners -- was supposed to showcase economic, political and cultural links between the two regions launched in Barcelona in November 1995.

It has been totally overshadowed, however, by the Middle East peace crisis prompted by the Israeli government's decision to press ahead with a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem which sparked a wave of Palestinian protests.
The 15 EU foreign ministers on Tuesday held separate talks with Arafat and Levy to press for a meeting and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo later met privately with both men.
The EU effort mirrors attempts by Washington to bring Israel and the Palestinians together, with U.S. envoy Dennis Ross due in the Middle East on Wednesday for meetings with both sides.
The Euro-Med conference was scheduled to resume at 0700 GMT with political statements from nine countries still to be heard.
On Tuesday van Mierlo, the conference chairman, gave extra time to the Palestinians and Israelis to put their views, and also to Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf as spokesman for the Arab group.

Arafat and Levy had briefly shaken hands during a reception hosted by Maltese Prime Minister Alfred Sant -- the highest level contact since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave the go-ahead for the settlement last month.
But the rancour returned as they addressed the conference.

"With the current Israeli government we have faced many obstacles and impediments," Arafat said. "Instead of continuing to build and reinforce fruitful cooperation and mutual respect...the Israeli government continues its settlement policy.
"We have been running around in closed circles without reaching any kind of positive agreement."

In response, Levy appealed for "the Palestinian Authority to broadcast, to publicise an unequivocably clear message against terrorism, refuting terrorism, returning to the dialogue, making the peace objective a common goal"
European Commission spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said early on Wednesday delegations were still working on the wording of a final declaration which had caused some divisions.
Algeria's foreign minister Attaf said they wanted a reference to the Middle East stalemate in the final statement, but EU officials said they would try to avoid this.
